exposure: demographics (prematurity, low birth weight, gestational age, birth weight)
treatment modalities (surfactant therapy, non-invasive ventilation, invasive mechanical ventilation)
outcome: neonatal morbidity (pulmonary hemorrhage, patent ductus arteriosus, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, septicemia, hypoglycemia, NICU stay length)
cohort: The study included 200 neonates admitted to the NICU with confirmed Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS).
finding: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS) remains a significant burden, with prematurity, low birth weight, cesarean delivery, and inadequate antenatal steroid coverage identified as key determinants of morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean section deliveries constituted 65% of the cohort and were identified as a key determinant of neonatal morbidity and mortality.
birth_weight: The cohort included neonates of varying birth weights, with 57.5% having low birth weight (<1500 g).
gest_age: The cohort included neonates of varying gestational ages, with 60% being preterm (<34 weeks gestation).
